name: Subclip
tagline: Transcript-first video editor for subtitles, clipping, dubbing, and social exports

pricing.notes: The Creator plan includes 600 AI credits per month. Transcription, subtitle generation, silence removal, and video exports are unlimited; cloud AI features consume credits and eligible plans can continue with pay-per-use.

verdictSummary: A local transcript-first cutter with silence removal, styled subtitles, and social exports is a credible weekend build. Matching Subclip's production dubbing and voice consistency, AI clip selection, browser media reliability, NLE exports, and publishing workflow takes substantially more work.
coreLoopDIY: Import a video, transcribe it locally, cut by editing the transcript or removing silence, style subtitles, and export a social-ready MP4 and SRT.
replacementScope: personal transcript-based video cutter and subtitle editor
requirements: desktop with enough storage for source media and renders
whatYouLose: production-grade dubbing and reusable voice cloning
motion graphics and deeper timeline editing
browser media pipeline polish and support
moatNotes: media workflow, cloud voice models, and publishing integrations
whyPeopleStillPay: Creators pay to avoid codec and rendering failures, get consistent long-form dubbing and reusable voices, move quickly from transcript to finished video, and export into the editing and publishing tools they already use.
ongoingBurden: Maintain transcription models, codecs, render performance, subtitle timing, browser compatibility, storage cleanup, model providers, and publishing APIs.

prompt:
Build me a local transcript-first video editor to replace Subclip for solo creator work. Requirements:

- Use Python 3.12 + FastAPI for a localhost web app, with a plain JavaScript frontend,
  FFmpeg for media work, and faster-whisper for word-level transcription.
- I can import MP4, MOV, WebM, MP3, or WAV files, see a synced transcript beside the
  video preview, and click any word to seek to its timestamp.
- Deleting transcript ranges creates an undoable cut list. Detect silences longer than
  500 ms and let me accept or reject each suggested cut before rendering.
- Let me edit subtitle text and timing, import or export SRT, and apply one ASS style
  file with font, colors, outline, position, and words-per-line controls.
- Export MP4 in 16:9, 9:16, or 1:1 with center-crop or blur-pad. Never overwrite the
  source, and show FFmpeg progress plus a useful failure message.
- Store projects as JSON under ~/SubclipDIY/projects and renders under
  ~/SubclipDIY/exports, with a recent-projects page and a delete-project action.
- Bind to localhost only. No accounts, uploads, telemetry, or network calls after the
  faster-whisper model has been downloaded.
- Out of scope: voice cloning, AI dubbing, viral-moment ranking, cloud sync, direct
  publishing, motion graphics, and a full nonlinear timeline.
- Add unit tests for cut-list merging and subtitle grouping, plus one smoke test that
  imports a short fixture and produces a playable MP4.
- Include a README with setup for Python and FFmpeg, model-size guidance, data paths,
  supported formats, and an honest warning about CPU transcription and render speed.
